newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer as dollar strengthens.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer as dollar strengthens.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened firmer on Thursday, rebounding from Wednesday's sharp drop, as a strengthening currency prompted widespread buying, dealers said.

"It's all dollar-related. It seems like there are buyers of Canada here," said one dealer. "There's some foreign (buying), some account driven. I think foreigners think with spot hovering around C$1.36 (US$0.7353) it was a good buying opportunity."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.0 percent from 3.08 percent at Wednesday's close.
Canada's dollar strengthened this morning to C$1.3564 (US$0.7372) from Wednesday's close of C$1.3608 (US$0.7349) buoyed in part by corporate buying.
T-bill dealers said a rebound in Canadian and U.S. bond markets, as well as the strengthening currency, helped to buoy the Canadian market.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued bill firmed to yield 3.25 percent from 3.35 percent. The one-year when-issued bill firmed to yield 3.63 percent from 3.76 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.15 percent, near the top of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
